fundamentals.name: Arm Holdings plc
fundamentals.longBusinessSummary: Arm Holdings plc researches, develops, licenses, and markets central processing unit (CPU) intellectual property (IP), graphics processing unit IP, systems IP, compute subsystems (CSS), and associated software, tools and related services. The company provides a product portfolio, including CPU IP, GPU and neural processing unit (NPU) accelerators, system IP such as interconnects, compute platform products including pre-integrated CSSs, and development tools and software. The company serves semiconductor companies, original equipment manufacturers (OEMs), cloud service providers (CSPs), and organizations developing chips for end markets such as smartphones, consumer electronics, industrial IoT, embedded systems, cloud data centers, networking, automotive, and robotics. It provides its products and services in the United States, China, Japan, Taiwan, Korea, and internationally. The company was founded in 1990 and is based in Cambridge, United Kingdom. Arm Holdings plc operates as a subsidiary of SoftBank Group Corp.

judgment.summary: High-growth company with exceptional margins and strong cash flow, but trades at a very high valuation and carries significant debt relative to equity.
judgment.earningsRecap: Last quarter beat EPS estimate by 3.6%; next earnings date is 2026-07-29.
positives: Revenue growth 20.1% YoY and earnings growth 47.9% YoY indicate strong top and bottom-line expansion.
Gross margin of 97.5% and operating margin of 29.5% are industry-leading.
Strong free cash flow of $750.50M (TTM) and a healthy current ratio of 6.00 suggest good liquidity.
Analyst growth estimates for the current quarter (14.4%) and fiscal year (22.5%) remain positive.
negatives: Trailing P/E of 408.70 and Forward P/E of 114.82 indicate an extremely high valuation.
Price/Sales (TTM) of 76.30 and Price/Book of 45.14 are also very elevated.
Debt/Equity ratio of 5.93 is high, suggesting significant leverage.
Beta of 3.79 indicates high volatility relative to the market.

news.paragraph: Arm Holdings is facing significant headwinds, with recent analyses suggesting its intrinsic value is far below its current market price, and a prominent bull case is being questioned due to AI chip selloffs and rate jitters. Insiders have sold substantial amounts of stock, and the company has been a leading factor in broad tech selloffs, contributing to Nasdaq-100 declines. The stock's recent volatility and insider selling suggest caution, despite a high analyst growth estimate for the current fiscal year.
